regions.name: Middle East
overview: The Yemen war crossed a strategic threshold when the Houthis captured the Yemeni side of Bab al-Mandeb on 10 September — Mokha, Hays, Al Khawkhah and the Hanish/Perim islands — giving the group direct control over one of the world's key chokepoints alongside its existing Red Sea leverage; Saudi-backed government forces have counter-attacked but the group's momentum, and the stakes for Riyadh, Cairo's Suez recovery and global shipping, have sharply increased.

The US-Iran war remains a grinding, multi-front stalemate: Hormuz tanker incidents (a US drone strike off Hormozgan, a disputed mine/missile attack on the supertanker El Gaia) and intermittent Iranian missile strikes on Jordan, Iraq and Saudi Arabia continue on a near-weekly cadence, while a third US House vote to end the war and 200 days of silence from presumed successor Mojtaba Khamenei both signal mounting strain without yet shifting the operational trajectory.

Disarmament processes in Lebanon and Iraq are advancing on paper while stalling in practice: Beirut's cabinet-approved Hezbollah disarmament plan is moving toward a contested 'phase two' south of the Litani, and Baghdad officials are already reframing Iraq's 30 September militia deadline as a mere coalition-withdrawal date rather than a binding disarmament requirement, with Iran-aligned armed actors in both countries retaining weapons as leverage.

Israel's simultaneous management of Gaza, Lebanon, Syria, the West Bank and its Iran-alliance commitments is increasingly shaped by the 27 October election calendar: record West Bank settler violence, near-daily Gaza strikes and a sharply intensified pace of ground incursions into southwestern Syria (Quneitra/Daraa, roughly 45 operations in two weeks) are all trending upward, while China's Xi Jinping used a first-in-a-decade Cairo visit to press a 'new Middle East security order' and expand investment as the war's duration opens diplomatic space for outside powers.

countries.name: Gaza
incidents: 10 Sep — Beit Lahiya: An Israeli strike killed at least 4, including two children, as the IDF said it hit Hamas weapons-storage sites in three separate areas of the Strip.
13 Sep — Gaza City (Tal al-Hawa): An Israeli drone strike on a vehicle killed 2 and wounded 13.
14 Sep — Gaza-wide: The Gaza Health Ministry put the cumulative post-ceasefire toll at 1,344 killed, including roughly 315 children and 160 women.
Mid-Sep — Gaza-wide: UN officials voiced 'deep concern' over continued Israeli strikes killing civilians despite the nominal ceasefire framework.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The ceasefire remains nominally in force while Israeli strikes against declared Hamas infrastructure and personnel continue at a near-daily tempo, sustaining a slow-burn casualty rate of roughly 15–20 killed per week. Absent a renegotiated enforcement mechanism, UN and humanitarian pressure will intensify but is unlikely to alter Israeli operational calculus, particularly as the government prioritizes military messaging ahead of the 27 October election. Watch for a possible spike in tempo tied to hostage-related developments or a deliberate signal to Hamas during Israel's wider multi-front posture against Iran-aligned actors.

countries.name: Lebanon
incidents: Early Sep — South Lebanon: Israeli dawn air strikes on Nabatieh and surrounding towns killed at least 10, part of a sustained campaign that has left the south's former economic hub largely emptied.
5 Sep — Beirut: The cabinet approved the LAF's multi-phase 'Homeland Shield' disarmament plan starting south of the Litani; five Shiite ministers walked out before the vote.
Mid-Sep — South Lebanon: Schools reopened on 15 September, many still doubling as shelters for residents displaced by ongoing strikes.
Mid-Sep — Tehran/Beirut: Iran's Security Council secretary publicly pledged continued support to Hezbollah to resist disarmament pressure, underscoring Tehran's stake in the outcome.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Expect the dual-track pattern to continue — Israeli strikes on Hezbollah military infrastructure in the south persisting near-weekly, while the LAF cautiously advances toward a 'phase two' (the Litani–Awali buffer zone) that Hezbollah has already rejected in principle. Iranian rhetorical and possibly material backing for Hezbollah raises the risk of the group testing the LAF's resolve or Israel's redlines, particularly if Tehran seeks a diversionary front amid its own war posture. A negotiated Israeli withdrawal from occupied Lebanese territory remains unlikely within this horizon.

countries.name: Iran
incidents: 14 Sep — Off Hormozgan: A US drone struck two boats, killing most aboard; Iranian media described the target as fishing vessels.

13–14 Sep — Strait of Hormuz: The supertanker El Gaia caught fire; Iran claimed a naval mine, while US CENTCOM said the vessel had been hit by an Iranian missile the prior month and then struck again by drone.

17 Sep — UN Security Council: A vote on restoring the 1737 sanctions committee was scheduled, with Russia and China opposing reestablishment and Iran's envoy protesting denial of access as an 'abuse of power.'
15 Sep — Tehran: Presumed successor Mojtaba Khamenei marked 200 days in his post with no public appearance, video or statement, feeding uncertainty over succession and central command authority.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Expect continued low-to-mid-intensity maritime and proxy warfare rather than decisive escalation or ceasefire — tanker seizures/strikes in Hormuz, contested mine claims, and intermittent missile strikes on US and allied positions across Iraq, Jordan and the Gulf states. A third US House vote to end the war signals growing domestic political friction that could eventually constrain Washington but has not yet altered operational tempo. Continued opacity around Mojtaba Khamenei's role is a wildcard: a leadership vacuum or contested succession could accelerate internal regime instability or trigger a hardline escalation to project strength. Rial depreciation and roughly 90% inflation will continue to erode regime capacity to sustain the conflict, raising medium-term regime-stability risk.

countries.name: Yemen
incidents: 10 Sep — Hodeidah/Taiz coast: Houthi forces captured the Hays and Al Khawkhah districts and the port town of Mokha, along with Perim (Mayun) Island, giving them direct control of the Yemeni side of the Bab al-Mandeb strait for the first time.

13 Sep — Red Sea coast: Saudi-backed government forces launched counter-attacks, including airstrikes on Houthi positions at Mokha and Dhubab in Taiz province, after conceding what officials called a 'painful' defeat.

14 Sep — Saudi border: The Houthis claimed a large-scale missile/drone attack on King Khalid Air Base near Khamis Mushait, in stated retaliation for over 300 Saudi airstrikes across Yemen in the preceding five days.
Ongoing — Nationwide: The UN estimates more than 80,000 people displaced by fighting since the start of September, as the country risks sliding back into full civil war.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, escalating within the band. The Houthi capture of Mokha and the Hanish/Perim islands marks a strategic inflection: the group now holds physical leverage over one of the world's key chokepoints alongside its established threat to Hormuz-adjacent traffic, materially raising the stakes for Saudi Arabia, Egypt and global shipping insurers. Expect continued Saudi-Yemeni government efforts to reclaim Red Sea coastal positions, met by further Houthi missile/drone strikes deeper into Saudi territory (Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan, possibly Riyadh-area targets). A negotiated de-escalation is unlikely within 90 days given the scale of recent Houthi gains; watch for formal Houthi blockade enforcement against Saudi-linked shipping and further internationalization of the conflict if Western naval assets intervene to protect the strait.

countries.name: Israel
incidents: Ongoing — West Bank: Settler violence continues at an average of roughly 6.6 incidents a day, on pace to exceed 2,000 attacks for 2026 — the highest rate on record per UN monitoring.

Ongoing — West Bank: Sustained settlement expansion and demolitions have displaced or partially displaced 107 Palestinian communities since January 2023, with the pace accelerating ahead of the election.
Ongoing — Multi-front: Israel remains simultaneously engaged in Gaza, Lebanon, southwest Syria and, via the US alliance, the Iran/Yemen war, with no negotiated resolution on any front.

Campaign period — Nationwide: Netanyahu's campaign for the 27 October election centers on hostage returns and military achievements, while challenger Gadi Eisenkot positions around war-management competence; the outcome could shape near-term escalation or de-escalation choices on every front.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Expect settler violence to remain at or above record levels through the October election as political incentives favor visible facts-on-the-ground in the West Bank, with a material risk of a mass-casualty incident triggering wider unrest. Militarily, Israel will likely sustain its current operational tempo in Gaza and southwest Syria while calibrating Lebanon strikes to LAF disarmament progress. The election itself is the dominant variable: a Netanyahu win likely preserves the current multi-front posture, while an Eisenkot-led coalition could seek negotiated off-ramps on at least one front — most plausibly Lebanon — without substantially altering the Iran or Gaza postures within this window.

countries.name: Iraq
incidents: 14 Sep — Sulaimani province: Five missiles struck three sites (a Komala family camp at Zirgwez, near Gurgachya on the Sirwan, and the Qaradagh area) in the early hours; no casualties reported.
15 Sep — Erbil province (Soran district): A one-way attack drone struck a KDPI base at Balisan; material damage only, no casualties.

15 Sep — Baghdad: Iran-aligned militias (Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada) signaled their weapons will not be surrendered by the 30 September deadline as the last US troops prepare to withdraw.

Mid-Sep — Baghdad: Iraq's National Security Advisor clarified that 30 September marks the coalition's departure date rather than a binding disarmament deadline, confirming the deadlock; the IRGC-Quds Force reportedly instructed militia leaders to retain weapons as leverage against Washington while avoiding direct confrontation with Iraqi security forces.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The 30 September deadline is highly unlikely to produce genuine militia disarmament; expect it to pass with rhetorical commitments, partial or symbolic handovers by weaker factions, and continued retention of heavy weapons by the core IRGC-aligned groups. Strikes on Iranian-Kurdish opposition targets in the KRI, as seen this week, will likely continue intermittently, distinct from and lower-intensity than direct anti-US strikes. The central risk within this window is a renewed direct militia attack on US positions timed either to the deadline's passage or to a broader Iranian signaling need, which would sharply escalate Iraq's role in the wider war.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
incidents: 14 Sep — Khamis Mushait/Abha/Taif: Houthi ballistic missile and drone attacks injured 13 civilians and damaged seven homes and two vehicles; the Houthis claimed a large-scale strike on King Khalid Air Base, asserting damage to hangars, radar, runways and ammunition depots.
15 Sep — Mecca approach: Saudi air defenses detected and destroyed a drone south of Mecca before it entered restricted airspace.

Ongoing — Yemen: The Saudi-led coalition sustained an air campaign against Houthi positions, with Houthi sources claiming over 300 strikes in the five days preceding 14 September, including repeated hits on Sadaa.
Ongoing — Southwestern border: Continued rocket/drone alert postures across Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran reflect a persistent, multi-axis Houthi threat to Saudi territory.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The tanker-war-adjacent exchange between Riyadh and the Houthis is likely to intensify rather than subside, driven directly by the Houthi capture of Bab al-Mandeb and Saudi Arabia's determination to prevent a Houthi-controlled chokepoint from becoming a permanent strategic fact. Continued Saudi airstrikes into Yemen will likely be met with further long-range missile/drone attacks against southwestern Saudi cities, with oil infrastructure further north (Jeddah, Jizan, Riyadh-area targets) not ruled out. Coalition-building with the internationally recognized Yemeni government to reclaim Red Sea coastal positions is the most likely near-term Saudi objective, though success within 90 days is uncertain given recent Houthi momentum.

countries.name: Syria
incidents: 15–16 Sep — Suwayda: Fresh clashes between government-aligned security forces and the Druze National Guard militia erupted around Mazraa and spread across the western/northern countryside; one militia fighter killed, roughly 10 internal security personnel wounded.
13 Sep — Quneitra: Israeli forces raided al-Rufayd and al-Hamadiyah villages overnight, detaining at least three local men.
16 Sep — Daraa (Yarmouk River Basin): Israeli troops raided the town of Abdin, searching homes and confiscating residents' mobile phones; no casualties reported.

First half of Sep — Quneitra/Daraa: Israel conducted an estimated 45 distinct ground operations into southwestern Syria in the first two weeks of the month alone, alongside a rising rate of artillery strikes, some hitting residential areas.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The Suwayda ceasefire remains effectively nominal, with recurring low-casualty flare-ups between Druze militias and Damascus-aligned forces continuing on a roughly weekly cadence, sustained by deep mistrust following last year's mass-casualty violence. Israel's ground-incursion tempo into Quneitra and Daraa is trending upward with no sign of near-term restraint, functioning as both a security buffer-building exercise and an implicit deterrent against any Damascus move to reassert control near the Golan. Watch for a more serious Suwayda flashpoint that could again draw a direct Israeli air response, as occurred in July 2025.

countries.name: Egypt
incidents: 2 Sep (effects ongoing) — Cairo: Xi Jinping made his first state visit to Egypt in a decade, meeting Sisi and calling for a 'new Middle East security order' free of external interference; Chinese investment in Egypt is now estimated near $10 billion.

Mid-Sep — Cairo: Sisi said Suez Canal revenues have fallen by roughly $9 billion over the past two years due to regional instability, even as FY2025/26 revenue rose 23% year-on-year to $4.67 billion amid a partial, fragile recovery.
No direct kinetic incident on Egyptian territory was identified for the 10–17 September window.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Egypt's core exposure remains economic rather than kinetic. The Houthi capture of the Yemeni side of Bab al-Mandeb on 10 September is a material new downside risk to the nascent Suez Canal traffic recovery Sisi has been counting on for H2 2026 — a prolonged Houthi blockade posture could reverse the 23% revenue gain rather than allow the further improvement officials have projected. China's high-profile investment push offers Cairo a partial economic cushion and diplomatic hedge, but is unlikely to offset canal revenue losses within this horizon. No change to Egypt's direct security posture is expected, but its role as a Gaza mediator and its Suez revenue trajectory should be watched closely as leading indicators of how the wider war is reshaping regional trade flows.

countries.name: Jordan
incidents: 9 Sep — Muwaffaq Salti air base, Azraq: Jordanian air defenses intercepted 18 of 20 Iranian ballistic missiles fired at the base; no injuries reported.
Late Aug (background) — Muwaffaq Salti: The same base absorbed direct hits in an earlier wave, damaging a Jordanian A-10 and roughly eight F-15s, illustrating its continued status as a live target.

10–17 Sep — Jordanian airspace: No further confirmed Iranian strike was identified in this window, suggesting a relative lull following the 9 September barrage, though this cannot be read as a durable pause given the pace of prior attacks.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Jordan remains a recurring secondary target for Iranian strikes against US assets at Muwaffaq Salti, and the apparent lull since 9 September should not be read as de-escalation given the volatility of the broader war. Expect continued high alert-status air-defense posture, with further Iranian barrages likely tied to US or Israeli actions elsewhere (Hormuz, Iraq, Yemen). Jordan's decision to keep its airspace open despite repeated targeting reflects a calculated bet on continued US/Jordanian interception effectiveness; a successful high-casualty strike would sharply raise both domestic political pressure and regional escalation risk.

countries.name: Libya
incidents: Late Aug – early Sep — Tripoli: Reports of militia buildup around the capital heightened fears of an imminent clash between forces aligned with PM Dbeibah and the Special Deterrence Force (RADA) militia.

Ongoing — Tripoli: Civil unrest driven by chronic power blackouts and collapsing municipal services has included blockades of government ministries and a shutdown of the strategically important Mellitah oil and gas complex.
Ongoing — Tripoli: US envoy Massad Boulos met PM Dbeibah to explore east-west military coordination, indicating active international engagement to prevent escalation.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained, with risk indicators trending upward. Libya's risk profile is rising within the band, driven by the convergence of a militia power struggle (Dbeibah vs. RADA) with genuine popular unrest over service failures — a combination that has historically preceded Tripoli clashes. The Mellitah shutdown is a notable escalation indicator given its economic significance. Absent a negotiated de-escalation, the Boulos mediation being the most concrete current effort, a limited armed confrontation in Tripoli within the next 90 days is plausible, though a full-scale return to civil war remains less likely given continued UNSMIL-brokered election-framework engagement.

countries.name: Tunisia
incidents: 4 Sep — Tunis: Journalist Mohamed Yousfi, editor-in-chief of investigative outlet Al-Qatiba, was arrested ahead of a scheduled radio appearance on charges of illicit enrichment and money laundering, widely seen as politically motivated.
~15 Sep — Tunis: Journalists and activists staged street protests demanding Yousfi's release, continuing a pattern of press-freedom demonstrations.

Ongoing — Nationwide: Protests continued over water and electricity cuts, rising prices and medicine shortages, compounding political grievances tied to President Saied's five-year-old emergency-rule consolidation.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Expect continued low-intensity but persistent protest activity combining press-freedom and economic grievances, with periodic journalist and activist arrests under the 2022 'false news' decree sustaining international criticism without triggering a change in government posture. Saied's consolidation of power shows no sign of reversing; the more relevant risk indicator for this horizon is whether infrastructure-driven unrest scales into broader, sustained mobilization, which would be a more significant departure from the current pattern than the press-freedom protests alone.

regions.name: Ukraine/Russia
overview: No ceasefire, deepening mutual strike campaigns: Witkoff/Kushner shuttle diplomacy (Kyiv and Moscow, early September) produced no breakthrough and only a push for renewed trilateral talks, and both sides have doubled down militarily instead — Russia sustaining near-nightly barrages on Kyiv and Odesa's grid ahead of winter, and Ukraine executing its deepest-ever drone strikes into Russia's Arctic energy infrastructure alongside continued refinery strikes on Ryazan and Rostov.

War-driven fuel and energy stress is now a two-front story: Russia's domestic fuel crisis (roughly 70% of gasoline demand met, refining at a 24-year low) is colliding with the State Duma elections on 18–20 September, including illegal voting staged in occupied Ukrainian territory, just as Moldova approaches its own energy inflection point with the 30 September expiry of the Gazprom–Transnistria supply contract.

Governance fault lines are widening in Kyiv: the NABU/SAPO 'Operation Carthage' probe has now claimed a sitting Prosecutor General, Ruslan Kravchenko, dismissed by the Rada on 15 September, and continues to press toward Zelensky's inner circle, testing Ukraine's institutional resilience at the same moment Western partners are being asked for winter energy and air-defense support.

Democratic backsliding is intensifying on the EU's eastern edge ahead of key votes: Georgia's ruling party is moving to legally eliminate its last standing parliamentary opposition weeks before the 4 October local elections, while Belarus and Russia continue coordinated exercise activity and hybrid migration pressure has pivoted from Poland toward Latvia — a broadening, multi-vector pressure campaign against NATO's eastern flank and EU-aligned states beyond Ukraine itself.

countries.name: Ukraine
incidents: 8 Sep — Kyiv: The 5–8 September truce ordered around the Witkoff/Kushner shuttle visit expired; Russia resumed strikes, killing at least 5 and injuring 30 across five districts, as Ukraine's air force reported downing 142 drones and all but one of 32 cruise missiles.
15 Sep — Kyiv: A Russian drone attack on a filling station killed at least 1 and injured 12, part of a sustained multi-night barrage on the capital.

15 Sep — Kyiv: The Verkhovna Rada voted 317–0 to dismiss Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko at Zelensky's request, after Kravchenko resigned on 7 September amid the NABU/SAPO 'Operation Carthage' probe into a group allegedly bribed to protect fraudulent call centers; Kravchenko had separately moved to file charges against NABU Director Semen Kryvonos.

Early–mid Sep — Odesa region: Continued Russian strikes on port and energy infrastructure, following a 1–4 September wave that hit a thermal power plant and substations, consistent with a pre-winter campaign against Ukraine's grid.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Expect no negotiated ceasefire in the near term — the Witkoff/Kushner rounds produced only a push for renewed trilateral talks, with Zelensky publicly stating 'the war will continue.' Russia will sustain and likely intensify combined missile and drone strikes on Kyiv, Odesa and grid infrastructure through autumn as a pre-winter coercive campaign, while Ukraine continues deep strikes against Russian refining and energy targets. Domestically, the NABU/SAPO corruption probe has now claimed the Prosecutor General and continues to reach toward Zelensky's inner circle; watch for further senior resignations, coalition friction in the Rada, and Western donor scrutiny of governance just as winter-support and air-defense requests are being negotiated with Washington.

countries.name: Russia
incidents: 6 Sep — Ryazan/Rostov-on-Don: Ukrainian drones struck the Ryazan oil refinery and targeted multiple cities; explosions and a four-hour drone presence were reported over Rostov-on-Don.
9 Sep — Arctic Russia: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces conducted their deepest strike of the war to date, hitting a gas-processing plant roughly 2,700 km from the border.

Ongoing through Sep — Nationwide: The fuel crisis continues, with Russia meeting only around 70% of domestic gasoline demand, crude processing at a 24-year low (~3.6 million bpd), a fuel export ban still in force and dozens of regions maintaining purchase restrictions.

18–20 Sep — Nationwide and occupied Ukraine: State Duma elections, the first since the 2022 invasion, proceed under a near-total Kremlin lock on the outcome, with voting also staged in occupied Crimea, Sevastopol, Luhansk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson, condemned internationally as illegal.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. United Russia is set to retain its constitutional majority in a tightly managed Duma vote, but the election lands against an unprecedented, war-driven fuel crisis reaching ordinary Russians — a genuine, if still contained, source of domestic friction. Expect Moscow to continue prioritizing strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure to impose leverage ahead of winter while absorbing continued Ukrainian deep strikes on refineries and Arctic and Black Sea energy assets that will keep pressuring refining capacity and export flows. Political risk to the regime remains low in the short term, but sustained fuel and logistics strain, plus the illegitimate occupied-territory voting, will keep feeding both domestic discontent and Western sanctions and isolation narratives.

countries.name: Belarus
incidents: 15–18 Sep — Grodno/Brest Oblasts: Belarus conducted 'defensive' military drills near the Polish and Lithuanian borders, officially framed around border protection, counter-sabotage and counter-drone training.
14 Sep — Lithuania: Lithuania launched its own military exercises across 12 municipalities in response to continued Russian and Belarusian probing of NATO's eastern border.

Late Sep (upcoming) — Russia: CSTO's 'Interaction-2026' command-and-staff exercise, part of the broader 'Indestructible Brotherhood' drill series involving 5,000-plus personnel, is scheduled at a Russian Central Military District training ground.

Ongoing — Latvia: Migrant-trafficking pressure via Belarus has shifted toward Latvia (111 attempted crossings reported in one week) while Poland's Belarus-border crossings have fallen over 98% year-on-year due to hardened security measures.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Belarus continues to function primarily as a facilitation and pressure platform for Moscow rather than an independent escalation risk. Expect continued Belarusian and CSTO exercise activity through October, culminating in Interaction-2026, sustained low-level drone transits toward EU airspace, and a redirected hybrid migration campaign now concentrating on Latvia rather than Poland — prompting further Baltic-state border hardening and NATO eastern-flank reinforcement rhetoric. There is no indication of Belarusian forces entering direct combat operations.

countries.name: Moldova
incidents: Ongoing — Chisinau: Moldova's Energy Ministry confirmed the country will not return to its old Gazprom/Transnistria energy model as the 30 September 2026 expiry of the Moldovagaz–Transnistria supply contract approaches, with a Swiss/Hungarian group already substituting as the effective gas supplier since 2025.

Ongoing — Nationwide: Continued Russian-linked hybrid pressure and disinformation activity is being countered by Moldova's Center for Strategic Communication and Combating Disinformation under President Sandu's office.

No major kinetic or political-crisis incident specific to 10–17 September was found; coverage this week is dominated by forward-looking analysis of the Gazprom contract deadline rather than new events.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. The approaching 30 September Gazprom–Transnistria contract expiration is the key near-term flashpoint — a lapse without a negotiated replacement risks renewed energy-supply disruption in Transnistria and associated humanitarian and political pressure on Chisinau, which Moscow could exploit for hybrid destabilization. Absent a specific trigger, expect continued low-intensity disinformation and influence operations rather than overt escalation; monitor closely for the Gazprom/Moldovagaz negotiation outcome and Transnistrian authorities' response in the final days of September.

countries.name: Georgia
incidents: 16 Sep — Tbilisi: Georgian Dream expanded its Constitutional Court suit to seek a ban on 'For Georgia,' the last major opposition party still holding parliamentary-threshold status, extending an earlier push against four other parties and threatening to outlaw the entire organized opposition ahead of the 4 October local elections.

Ongoing — Tbilisi: Rustaveli Avenue protests continue past the 650-day mark despite the extended crackdown; PACE and international observers continue to state that conditions for genuinely democratic elections do not currently exist in Georgia.

Run-up to 4 Oct — Nationwide: Local elections approach under an ongoing opposition-ban campaign, prior 'coup attempt' charges against opposition leaders from the 2025 election cycle, and continued detentions of protest organizers.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Georgian Dream is very likely to press forward with Constitutional Court bans on remaining opposition parties in the immediate run-up to the 4 October local elections, further narrowing the political field and likely triggering renewed mass protest activity around the election date itself. Expect continued detentions and prosecutions of opposition and civil-society figures, sustained Western criticism without material policy consequences, and a real possibility of a significant flashpoint on or immediately after 4 October, consistent with the pattern from the October 2025 election cycle. The level should be watched for a possible upgrade to CRITICAL around the election date if unrest intensifies.

countries.name: Armenia
incidents: 1 Sep — Bishkek: Pashinyan and Putin met on the SCO summit sidelines for roughly an hour, discussing Armenia's EU-accession intentions — a notable public airing of Yerevan's West-leaning shift directly with Moscow.

9 Sep — Yerevan: Reporting indicated Pashinyan instructed allies to temporarily freeze anti-Russian rhetoric, suggesting a tactical recalibration in Yerevan's balancing act between Moscow, Washington and Brussels.

Mid-Sep — Yerevan: Reports of upheaval within Armenia's state security apparatus followed the August dismissal of Security Council Secretary Armen Grigoryan; Pashinyan's campaign against Catholicos Karekin II and the Apostolic Church leadership continues.

15 Sep (adjacent) — Yerevan: Armenia's Constitutional Court was expected to rule on the US-backed TRIPP transit corridor ahead of a parliamentary vote; Azerbaijan's foreign minister has acknowledged construction will not start until 2027, later than originally planned.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Armenia continues to advance the Azerbaijan peace/TRIPP track diplomatically even as the corridor's physical implementation slips into 2027, while simultaneously managing a delicate, multi-vector balancing act with Russia and the West. Domestically, the Pashinyan–Church confrontation and signs of turnover in the security apparatus are the most likely sources of near-term political volatility; watch for further personnel changes, Church-related mobilization by religious conservatives, and any Azerbaijani reaction to delays in TRIPP's construction timeline.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
incidents: Ongoing — Baku/Moscow: Aliyev's declaration of full normalization between Russia and Azerbaijan continues to hold, with no new border or aviation incidents identified for the 10–17 September window.

Ongoing — Baku/Yerevan: Azerbaijan continues engagement on the TRIPP corridor and broader peace process with Armenia, though Baku's own foreign minister has confirmed construction will not begin until 2027, a modest slippage from the original target.
No new incident specific to the 10–17 September period was identified beyond the above; reporting for this window remains limited, consistent with the country's de-escalated posture.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Azerbaijan's trajectory remains stable and de-escalatory: continued normalization with both Russia and Armenia, with Baku positioned as a relative beneficiary of the TRIPP process despite its delayed construction start. The main risks over the next 90 days are exogenous — a stalling or collapse of the Armenia peace process, a resurgence of Russia-Azerbaijan friction, or spillover tension tied to Armenia's internal instability. Absent such a trigger, no threat-level change is warranted.

regions.name: Sahel
overview: Economic warfare remains JNIM's primary jihadist tool: the group destroyed roughly 20 more fuel tankers in a 13-14 September ambush on the Kayes-Nioro axis, extending a blockade on Bamako now in its second year with over 300 tankers burned cumulatively, while ACLED assesses the same 'economic warfare' tactic is spreading toward mining infrastructure and coastal West Africa (Togo, Benin, northern Ghana).

Juntas are responding to internal threats with repression rather than reform: Niger's post-mutiny purge deepened with a military reshuffle and a 30-month prison sentence for a journalist over a WhatsApp clip, illustrating a regional pattern — also visible in Mali and Burkina Faso — where regime security and information control take priority over transparent counter-insurgency reporting.

Sudan's North Kordofan campaign continues to escalate and threatens wider Sahel-adjacent spillover: SAF is consolidating an El Obeid-Bara-Dilling corridor after seizing Hamrat al-Wiz, while RSF sustains drone strikes on civilian infrastructure in El Obeid amid a worsening cholera outbreak, with the war's momentum keeping Chad's eastern border on maximum alert.

Negotiated de-escalation with one jihadist faction is leaving rival factions as the primary residual threat: Nigeria's reported secret ceasefire with Boko Haram/JAS explicitly excludes ISWAP, which remains a reprisal-attack risk around Lake Chad even as unabated north-west banditry — a Bello Turji-linked raid killing roughly 10 and abducting 40 in Sokoto's Tofa area — continues to drive the bulk of national fatalities.

countries.name: Mali
incidents: 13–14 Sep — Kayes-Nioro du Sahel axis: JNIM/FLM fighters ambushed a military-escorted convoy of roughly 40 fuel tankers between Kaniera and Lakamane, setting multiple vehicles ablaze; at least 20 tankers were destroyed.
15 Sep — Bamako/Kayes: FAMa said troops 'responded forcefully' to the ambush, underscoring the army's continued reliance on armed escorts to move fuel.

Ongoing — Bamako: The JNIM blockade, in place since September 2025, persists into its second year; over 300 tankers have now been burned nationwide, with the capital still dependent on convoy resupply and experiencing rationing and reduced street lighting.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. JNIM will almost certainly sustain and periodically intensify convoy interdiction on the Kayes-Nioro and Kayes-Bamako axes, using the blockade as leverage for political and religious demands while avoiding a full urban assault on the capital. FAMa/Africa Corps escorted convoys will continue to get fuel through at high cost, preventing total collapse but not restoring normal supply; expect further tanker losses, rising fuel and food prices, and growing strain on Bamako's basic services. Watch for blockade tactics spreading further toward the Senegal, Mauritania and Guinea borders and mining infrastructure, consistent with JNIM's stated economic-warfare strategy.

countries.name: Niger
incidents: 7 Sep — Niamey: Police arrested Ali Soumana, editor-in-chief of weekly Le Courrier, on defamation-related charges after his paper alleged customs fraud involving the Prime Minister.
11 Sep — Niamey: Junta leader Tiani signed a decree appointing Brigadier General Mamane Sani Kiaou as new armed forces chief of staff, part of the post-mutiny military reshuffle.
16 Sep — Niamey: A court sentenced Hassane Zada, an editor at Toubal Info and Canal 3 correspondent, to 30 months in prison and a fine over a WhatsApp audio clip deemed insulting to Tiani.
Ongoing — Nationwide: The purge following the 28-29 August coup attempt continues, with dozens of soldiers and officials, including former defence minister Kalla Moutari, detained.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The junta will almost certainly continue consolidating control through military reshuffles, arrests and judicial intimidation of the press rather than through political liberalization, reflecting persistent distrust within the officer corps after the August mutiny. This repression-driven stabilization is likely to hold Niamey secure in the near term but risks deepening resentment among mid-tier officers, keeping the coup-within-the-coup risk elevated. Concurrently, JNIM/ISSP pressure in Tillaberi is expected to continue largely unabated, as security resources remain partly absorbed by internal purge and regime-protection activity rather than counter-insurgency operations.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
incidents: 10–17 Sep — Nationwide: The severe reporting blackout persisted, with no verified, dated incident located for this specific window from major wire services or regional outlets — itself an information-vacuum indicator rather than a sign of calm.

Background — Sebba/Titao/Djibo axis: Government forces have claimed intensified offensive operations against JNIM-affiliated fighters, claims that remain difficult to independently verify given the reporting environment.

Background — Nationwide: ACLED's September assessment notes JNIM continues to blockade cities and besiege towns across Burkina Faso as part of a broader Sahel-wide economic-warfare campaign, while also expanding operations toward coastal West Africa.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Given the persistent absence of independently verifiable reporting, the JNIM-versus-Islamic State Sahel Province contest for Liptako-Gourma and the sieges of Djibo, Sebba and Titao should be assumed to be continuing at a high tempo rather than resolving. Government claims of battlefield gains should be treated cautiously pending independent confirmation. Analysts should prioritize satellite imagery, displacement data and cross-border refugee reporting from Mali, Niger, Ghana, Togo and Benin as proxy indicators of the security trajectory inside Burkina Faso.

countries.name: Sudan
incidents: 6 Sep — Hamrat al-Wiz, North Kordofan: SAF and allied forces seized the town from RSF, extending the army's defensive buffer around Jabrat al-Sheikh and Bara and securing the highway corridor toward Khartoum.
8 Sep — Um Rawaba, North Kordofan: An RSF drone strike hit a courthouse at peak hours, killing at least 13 and injuring 22 civilians, part of an ongoing drone campaign into the reporting period.

14 Sep — Addis Ababa: Sudan's Islamist Popular Congress Party and the SLM-AW faction agreed to broaden talks toward an inclusive civilian-led political settlement, a diplomatic track running parallel to the military escalation.

Ongoing — El Obeid: The city remains under RSF siege with continuing drone strikes on power, water and fuel infrastructure; roughly 1.3 million IDPs are sheltering there amid a worsening cholera outbreak.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, escalating. SAF is likely to continue consolidating and expanding its North Kordofan corridor (El Obeid-Bara-Dilling axis) following recent gains, while RSF will almost certainly respond with intensified drone strikes against civilian and logistics targets in El Obeid and along contested supply routes, sustaining a high civilian casualty and displacement rate. The Addis Ababa track suggests fragmenting political alignments among armed and political factions, but is unlikely to translate into a ceasefire within the next quarter given the momentum of the Kordofan campaign. Expect continued risk of siege dynamics in El Obeid comparable to el-Fasher, further mass displacement toward Chad and South Sudan, and growing pressure on humanitarian access.

countries.name: Chad
incidents: 10–17 Sep — Eastern border: No new dated cross-border strike or clash inside Chad was confirmed within the window; the most recent confirmed incidents remain from late August.
20 Aug (background, driving current posture) — Ennedi-Est: Sudanese aircraft and drones pursued and struck a vehicle convoy over 100 km inside Chadian territory.
Late Aug (background) — Near Tine, eastern border: A Sudanese air/drone strike on a fuel market killed 12 and wounded 7; Chad accused SAF of the strike.

Ongoing — Eastern border: Chad remains at its highest alert level, with roughly 100 armoured vehicles and signal-jamming trucks deployed near Tine; the border with Sudan remains effectively closed amid continued refugee inflows (Chad hosts over 1 million displaced, including 940,000-plus Sudanese refugees).
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Chad is likely to maintain its heightened military posture along the eastern border through the period, balancing deterrence against SAF/RSF spillover with efforts to avoid direct confrontation with Sudan's warring parties. Further cross-border strikes or incursions attributed to either SAF or RSF remain a realistic possibility given the intensity of the North Kordofan campaign just across the border, which could trigger renewed diplomatic protests or a further alert escalation. Refugee flows into Ouaddai and Ennedi are expected to continue at a steady-to-rising pace, sustaining humanitarian strain even absent a major new cross-border incident.

countries.name: Mauritania
incidents: Late Aug/early Sep — Nouadhibou, Rosso, Dakar: Roughly 1,046 migrants who survived Atlantic crossing attempts disembarked in distressed condition across three West African cities, part of a wave of boats intercepted or stranded en route to the Canary Islands.

Ongoing — Nationwide: The EU-backed deportation campaign continues, with rights groups reporting continued mass arrests, detention in poor conditions and summary removals of migrants to Mali and Senegal.

Ongoing — Hodh Chargui/eastern border: Continued arrival of Malian refugees fleeing JNIM's insurgency and fuel blockade adds to an existing population of over 300,000 Malians sheltering in the region.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Mauritania is likely to sustain its EU-backed interdiction and deportation posture along the Atlantic migration route, continuing to draw human-rights criticism without a substantive change in policy. Spillover risk from Mali's JNIM blockade and Kayes-region attacks remains the primary security variable to watch, given JNIM's demonstrated willingness to strike near the Senegal/Mauritania border; a direct JNIM incursion into Mauritanian territory cannot be ruled out but has not yet materialized. Refugee inflows from Mali are expected to continue rising gradually, adding pressure to Hodh Chargui absorption capacity.

countries.name: Nigeria
incidents: 7 Sep — Kaduna State (Giwa and surrounding districts): Bandits killed 5 and abducted 27 villagers in nighttime raids on farming settlements.
7 Sep — Tofa, Rabah LGA, Sokoto: Bandits linked to warlord Bello Turji raided the community overnight, killing at least 10 and kidnapping around 40 residents.
10–11 Sep — Zamfara State: Troops of Joint Task Force North West (Operation Fansan Yamma) foiled a bandit attack and rescued 3 kidnap victims in separate operations.

Ongoing — North-east: Reports first surfacing 7-9 September indicate a secret three-month ceasefire between the federal government and Boko Haram/JAS since June, tied to the release of 360 civilians abducted from Ngoshe; the truce may be extended roughly 40 more days but explicitly excludes ISWAP, which remains a reprisal-attack risk around Lake Chad.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. North-west banditry in Sokoto, Zamfara and Kaduna is expected to continue at a high, largely unabated tempo despite ongoing JTF operations, with Bello Turji-linked networks remaining a primary driver of mass-casualty raids and kidnap-for-ransom. The reported Boko Haram/JAS ceasefire, if it holds or is extended, may reduce attack frequency directly attributable to JAS in the north-east, but is a fragile and non-transparent arrangement vulnerable to public exposure or breakdown; ISWAP's exclusion from the deal keeps the Lake Chad basin at elevated risk of reprisal attacks as ISWAP seeks to assert primacy over its rival faction. Overall, expect continued high fatality counts nationally driven primarily by north-west banditry rather than north-east jihadist violence in the near term.

regions.name: Asia-Pacific
overview: South China Sea grey-zone coercion is intensifying and diversifying across three fronts simultaneously: China's 11 September declaration of a 'nature reserve' at Scarborough Shoal, continued suspected radar construction at Yagong Island in the Paracels, and sustained PLA/coast guard activity around Taiwan collectively show Beijing pressing multiple claims in parallel, while Vietnam's own record-pace Spratly build-out complicates the narrative of China as the sole reclamation actor.

Diplomatic friction with China is becoming more overt and less controlled: a 9 September Seoul Defense Dialogue incident, in which a Chinese attache's mid-speech memo to the Philippine defence secretary triggered a viral public rebuke, is a sign that grey-zone assertiveness is increasingly spilling into undiplomatic public confrontation and strengthening informal coordination among China's rivals.

Two of the region's most severe internal conflicts, Myanmar and Balochistan, continued to intensify rather than stabilize: Myanmar's junta sustained a mass-casualty air campaign against civilians, including a 12 September strike on two boarding schools in Kyauktaw that killed an estimated 23 students, while the Baloch insurgency set new weekly operational records against Pakistani security forces, including a 14 September ambush claiming 9 killed near Lasbela.

Korean Peninsula dynamics show a genuine bifurcation between diplomatic opening and military hardening: Seoul is actively pursuing a Trump-Kim summit, potentially tied to a November APEC visit, while North Korea simultaneously resumed short-range missile testing on 12 September, commissioned a second advanced guided-missile destroyer, and deepened alliance language with Moscow — pursuing dialogue readiness and military buildup as parallel, not competing, tracks.

countries.name: North Korea
incidents: 6 Sep — Wonsan: North Korea commissioned its second Choe Hyon-class guided-missile destroyer, Kang Kon, an 88-VLS-cell, roughly 5,000-tonne vessel, confirming continued rapid naval buildup with two more hulls under construction.

12 Sep — Wonsan area: North Korea fired several short-range ballistic missiles roughly 250 km into the East Sea, the first launch since 20 August, coming one day after a five-day US–South Korea–Japan trilateral maritime drill.
15 Sep — Pyongyang: Kim Jong Un told Putin, marking the DPRK's 78th founding anniversary, that he would 'expand and deepen' cooperation with Russia, reaffirming the mutual-defence pact framework.

Ongoing — Inter-Korean border: Seoul officials describe an 'unprecedented' DPRK fortification build-up, including mines and additional barbed wire, continuing in parallel with the renewed missile activity.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Expect the DPRK to continue calibrated missile testing timed to allied exercises while accelerating naval and DMZ fortification, using the Kim-Putin channel to formalize further troop or materiel contributions to Russia ahead of a possible November meeting. A Trump-initiated summit remains plausible around the November APEC window, but Pyongyang is likely to keep testing and naval commissioning as leverage rather than pause them for diplomacy; South Korea will continue pursuing 'dialogue plus deterrence,' limiting near-term escalation risk but not resolving the underlying arms trajectory.

countries.name: Myanmar
incidents: 7 Sep — Ye-U, Sagaing Region: Junta gyrocopters and an Mi-35P helicopter bombed a civilian vehicle-repair workshop near a market despite no fighting nearby, killing 7 civilians.
12 Sep — Kyauktaw Township, Rakhine State: A military jet bombed two private boarding schools overnight, killing an estimated 23 students.
1–15 Sep — Karenni State (Demoso, Loikaw, Shadaw): Sustained Myanmar Air Force strikes killed at least 11 civilians, including children.

2–15 Sep — Ngazun Township, Mandalay Region and Rakhine State: Daily junta drone, helicopter and jet attacks on forest areas sheltering displaced civilians killed 7 in Ngazun, while heavy fighting continued around Kyaukphyu and Sittwe.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, deteriorating. The junta will almost certainly continue and likely intensify air operations against civilian and resistance-held areas as it seeks to consolidate territory, with Kachin, Rakhine, Karenni and Sagaing remaining the primary flashpoints. Resistance forces will continue to interdict junta river and road resupply and hold captured ground, but junta air superiority will keep civilian casualties high and displacement rising. Expect continued deterioration with no negotiated de-escalation likely in this window.

countries.name: Pakistan
incidents: 14 Sep — Kashari/Wallapat, Lasbela: The BLA's Fateh Squad ambushed a Frontier Corps bomb disposal convoy with an IED followed by direct fire; the group claims 9 personnel killed, 11-plus wounded.

14 Sep — Lasbela, Jiwani, Mashkel, Kachhi: The BLA/Baloch Republican Guards claimed a coordinated wave of operations, including a convoy attack, arson at a lithium exploration site, and road blockades.
15 Sep — Malant, Tump: An IED strike hit a Frontier Corps vehicle; the BLA claims 3 FC personnel killed.

Ongoing — Afghan border: TTP attack tempo in 2026 is tracking above 2025's already record-setting pace, with Islamabad continuing to condition improved ties with the Taliban on verifiable action against TTP and BLA elements it says operate from Afghan soil.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The BLA/BRG campaign shows no sign of plateauing — expect continued near-daily IED and ambush operations against military convoys and CPEC-adjacent infrastructure across Lasbela, Kalat, Turbat, Mastung and Kachhi, alongside sustained but lower-intensity TTP pressure from the Afghan border. Pakistan-Afghanistan relations will likely remain strained without a substantive Taliban crackdown, keeping cross-border friction elevated. Security-force casualty rates are likely to remain among the highest recorded for this insurgency, with continued risk of mass-casualty urban attacks in Quetta or provincial capitals.

countries.name: India
incidents: 14–15 Sep — Tamenglong/Noney districts, Manipur: Suspected militants attacked villages, killing 4 people, including a couple, and injuring their 6-year-old son, part of the expanding Naga-Kuki-Zo violence.
14 Sep — Manipur: The Kuki-Zo Council warned that continued armed-group activity risks pushing Manipur 'to full-scale conflict.'

Ongoing — Kangpokpi district: Naga groups continue blocking the highway despite a 14 August Supreme Court directive to plan reopening; over 260 deaths and 60,000-plus displaced since the crisis began in 2023, with 34 deaths specifically since the Naga-Kuki violence started in February.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Expect continued low-level but lethal tit-for-tat attacks along the new Naga-Kuki-Zo fault line, compounding the unresolved Meitei-Kuki dimension, with highway blockades sustaining economic strangulation of Kuki-Zo areas. Central government intervention has so far been limited to judicial directives rather than security-force de-escalation measures; absent a stronger federal posture, the risk of further village-level arson and displacement will remain elevated through the period, with periodic spikes around any highway-reopening attempt.

countries.name: China
incidents: 9 Sep — Seoul Defense Dialogue: A Chinese embassy military attache handed a memo reasserting China's rejection of the 2016 UNCLOS arbitration ruling to Philippine Defense Secretary Teodoro mid-speech; he read it aloud and rebuked Beijing on stage, triggering a viral diplomatic spat.

11 Sep — Scarborough Shoal: China declared a 3,524-hectare 'nature reserve' encompassing the shoal; the Philippines called it a deceptive veneer for an illegitimate claim, and the US publicly rejected China's position on 12 September.

Late Aug–early Sep (continuing) — Yagong Island, Paracels: Satellite imagery shows apparent early-warning radar construction; Vietnam formally protested, and reported land reclamation at nearby Antelope Reef appears to have completed its first stage.

Mid-Sep — Taiwan Strait: Taiwan detected 4 PLA aircraft, 6 PLAN vessels and 2 China Coast Guard 'official ships' operating around the island in a single day, with two aircraft entering Taiwan's southwestern and eastern ADIZ.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. China will likely continue simultaneous, incremental coercion across Scarborough Shoal, the Paracels and the Taiwan Strait/Senkakus rather than concentrating pressure on one flashpoint, using administrative and legal measures alongside coast guard and PLA presence to normalize expanded control while staying below the threshold for open conflict. The Seoul memo incident suggests Beijing's diplomatic messaging is becoming more overt and less calibrated, raising the risk of further unforced errors that strengthen regional coordination against it.

countries.name: Taiwan
incidents: 27 Aug (effective into this period) — Taipei: The legislature passed the 2026 budget after a record 266-day delay, including roughly NT$63.4 billion (~US$7.6 billion) for domestically made drones, after rejecting the government's original special drone budget and substituting its own plan.

Mid-Sep — Around Taiwan: A single-day snapshot recorded 4 PLA aircraft, 6 navy vessels and 2 coast guard/official ships, with two aircraft crossing into the southwestern and eastern ADIZ; Taiwan's MND flagged continued PLA emphasis on strengthening island-landing and amphibious capabilities.
Ongoing — Overall PLA sortie volume around Taiwan has reverted toward pre-May-2024 baseline levels since early 2026, suggesting an adjustment in Beijing's coercion strategy rather than de-escalation.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Expect continued steady-state PLA presence, aircraft and vessel incursions and ADIZ transits, without a return to the 2024-25 surge tempo, alongside accelerating Taiwanese investment in asymmetric drone capability now that budget gridlock has eased. Cross-strait friction will likely remain centered on economic and administrative coercion and information operations rather than kinetic escalation in this window, with the domestic nuclear-referendum debate adding another politically charged variable tied to resilience-under-blockade planning.

countries.name: Philippines
incidents: 9 Sep — Seoul Defense Dialogue: A Chinese military attache delivered a note reasserting Beijing's nine-dash-line position to Defense Secretary Teodoro mid-speech; he read it aloud on stage and publicly rebuked China, a viral incident that further inflamed bilateral relations.

11 Sep — Scarborough Shoal: China's declaration of a 'nature reserve' over the shoal was rejected by the Philippines' National Maritime Council as an attempt to legalize an illegitimate claim, depriving Filipino fishers of traditional access.
12 Sep — Washington: US Secretary of State Rubio issued a statement backing the Philippines and rejecting China's Scarborough claim.

Ongoing — PLA Southern Theater Command reported forward-deploying light combat aircraft and air-defense frigates to the South China Sea, while China has installed multiple floating structures in and around Scarborough Shoal since the reserve declaration.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Expect continued high-frequency but sub-kinetic CCG/PLAN presence and infrastructure moves, including floating barriers, at Scarborough, paired with intensifying diplomatic confrontation following the Seoul incident. Manila will likely continue leaning on US and broader international backing to internationalize the dispute, while Beijing's more overt public messaging risks further unforced diplomatic missteps. The risk of a physical collision or blockade incident at Scarborough remains elevated given the pace of Chinese structure emplacement.

countries.name: South Korea
incidents: 7–9 Sep — Seoul: The Seoul Defense Dialogue convened roughly 1,200 military officials and experts; Defence Minister Ahn Gyu-back publicly called for a resumption of Trump-Kim talks, framing it as being about 'peace on the Korean Peninsula.'

Early Sep — Seoul: South Korea's National Intelligence Service assessed a Trump-Kim summit as 'possible at any time,' with reporting suggesting Trump may seek to meet Kim around a November APEC trip to China.
11 Sep — Conclusion of a five-day US–South Korea–Japan trilateral maritime exercise, followed one day later by North Korea's short-range ballistic missile launches.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Seoul will continue pursuing parallel tracks: active diplomatic encouragement of a Trump-Kim meeting, plausibly around the November APEC window, alongside continued trilateral deterrence exercises with the US and Japan. Expect North Korea to respond to further drills with calibrated missile tests, without derailing the diplomatic opening. The gap between rhetorical de-escalation and continued DMZ militarization on both sides will persist as the central risk indicator to watch.

countries.name: Vietnam
incidents: 28 Aug (protest continuing to resonate) — Hanoi: Vietnam's Foreign Ministry formally protested apparent Chinese construction, assessed as an early-warning radar site, on Yagong Island in the Paracels, demanding immediate cessation.
Early Sep — Analysis reporting highlighted that Chinese land reclamation at nearby Antelope Reef appears to have completed its first stage, roughly 16 km from Yagong.

Ongoing through Sep — Vietnam continues its own Spratly infrastructure build-out across 27 sites and 18 reefs, having added 534 acres in the past year and approaching parity with China's total historical reclamation in the Spratlys.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Vietnam will likely continue a dual-track approach — sustained formal diplomatic protest against Chinese Paracels construction while simultaneously accelerating its own Spratly militarization, which increasingly rivals China's in scale. This asymmetry is likely to become a more prominent regional talking point without triggering direct Vietnam-China confrontation in this window.

countries.name: Japan
incidents: Ongoing (baseline continuing into 2026) — Senkaku Islands: Chinese Coast Guard vessels have patrolled Senkaku-administered waters almost daily, a tempo regional trackers describe as sustained into 2026 following a record 357 days in the contiguous zone in 2025.

Background — Senkaku Islands: Japanese and Chinese coast guard vessels have faced off near the islands after Japan's coast guard moved to expel Chinese ships approaching a Japanese fishing boat, part of a standing confrontation pattern.

Ongoing — The broader Japan-China diplomatic dispute continues to color maritime friction, with PLA intelligence flights near Japan reported as a standing pattern rather than a discrete this-week event.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained; continue to watch for a possible upgrade. Expect the high-tempo but non-escalatory Chinese Coast Guard presence around the Senkakus to continue, with periodic close-quarters incidents remaining likely given the elevated baseline. The combination of record CCG presence, an unresolved diplomatic rift with Beijing, and PLA activity elsewhere in the region raises the probability of an upgrade-triggering incident in the coming weeks.

countries.name: Indonesia
incidents: Early Sep — Tembagapura district, Central Papua: Suspected TPNPB fighters fired on a 15-vehicle PT Freeport Indonesia convoy near Mile Point 60, hitting three vehicles; no casualties reported.
Ongoing — Indonesian authorities report boosting security around Freeport operations in response to escalating attacks on convoys.
Ongoing — TNI sweep-and-drone operations in Intan Jaya and Puncak Jaya continue at a similar tempo to prior months, though no newly confirmed September-dated strike was identified in this search.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Expect the TPNPB to continue harassment-style attacks on Freeport logistics convoys in the Tembagapura/Mile Point corridor, prompting further TNI security reinforcement rather than a change in the campaign's character. The broader TNI sweep-and-drone campaign in Intan Jaya/Puncak likely continues at a similar tempo; maintain HIGH with a bias toward continued low-level attrition rather than a discrete escalation this period.

countries.name: Thailand
incidents: 15–16 Sep — Singapore: Thailand and Cambodia held the first meeting of a UN-backed compulsory conciliation process under UNCLOS over their long-running Gulf of Thailand maritime boundary dispute, with both foreign ministers delivering opening statements.

Context — Thailand entered the process 'in good faith' after having proposed direct bilateral talks first; Cambodia is seeking a single all-purpose maritime boundary treaty covering an area believed to hold roughly 12 trillion cubic feet of gas.

Background — Thailand terminated the 2001 joint development framework agreement in May 2026, a direct consequence of last year's deadly border clashes; the land-border ceasefire from 27 December 2025 continues to hold with no new violation reported this period.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained, with a de-escalation tilt. The Thailand-Cambodia relationship is likely to continue de-escalating on the ground while the maritime dispute shifts into a potentially lengthy UNCLOS conciliation process with an uncertain resolution timeline. Expect continued rhetorical sparring over process without a return to armed confrontation in this window; the land ceasefire remains the primary stability indicator to monitor.

countries.name: Bangladesh
incidents: Sep — Nationwide: A High Court ruling struck down two prior constitutional amendments, shifting judicial oversight responsibilities to the Supreme Court.

Ongoing — Nationwide: Human-rights reporting continues to describe an ongoing pattern of extralegal political violence and intimidation of religious and ethnic minorities under the BNP/Tarique Rahman government.
No specific dated Chittagong Hill Tracts clash or Awami League flash-protest event for the 10-17 September window could be verified in available reporting.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Absent a confirmed acute trigger this period, expect continued low-level, diffuse political violence tied to the post-Awami-League-ban political realignment and periodic Chittagong Hill Tracts indigenous-settler tension, without a clear escalatory event in the immediate term. Judicial and constitutional developments, including the September High Court ruling, may become a slower-burn source of political contestation over the coming months. Recommend continued monitoring given the historical volatility of the CHT and the anniversary-adjacent sensitivity around past September unrest.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
incidents: Recent — Maritime: Sri Lankan and US authorities seized approximately 463 kg of crystal methamphetamine from a Pakistan-based trafficking network, a law-enforcement issue rather than a security-threat escalation.
Ongoing — Colombo: Sri Lanka is hosting 'India Week 2026,' underscoring continued deepening of India-Sri Lanka ties under the NPP government.

Governance note — The ICC stripped Sri Lanka of hosting rights for the February 2027 Women's Champions Trophy over concerns about government interference in cricket administration; tourist arrivals fell 3.3% in August.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Sri Lanka's security environment is likely to remain stable, with organized-crime and narcotics interdiction and routine civil demonstrations as the principal ongoing activity rather than any resurgent conflict dynamic. The NPP government's continued tilt toward India, despite its historical anti-Indian orientation, is likely to persist as the notable strategic trend, alongside stable but not acute governance friction. No indicators support reversing the recent downgrade.

regions.name: Americas
overview: Drone warfare has become a defining threat vector across the northern Andes and Caribbean rim: Colombia's ELN is now conducting near-weekly explosive-drone swarm attacks against military and police targets in Norte de Santander and Cesar, prompting a roughly $1.68 billion national counter-drone program, while Venezuela's oil-and-security crisis and Ecuador's expanding US-backed counter-narcotics footprint suggest the region is converging on drone/counter-drone capability as the primary battlefield innovation of 2026.

US military and economic engagement is deepening and formalizing across multiple fronts simultaneously: beyond the ongoing Southern Spear boat-strike campaign against Venezuela (roughly 230 killed, still active) and the disputed 100-year Venezuelan oil concession, Washington has expanded Special Forces and naval deployments into Ecuador under the 'Shield of the Americas' coalition, indicating a broader, more permanent US security posture in the hemisphere.

State-of-emergency governance has become the default crisis-management tool across the region: Ecuador's new 60-day decree and coastal curfews, Peru's prison-focused emergency across five facilities and 17 districts, and Bolivia's 90-day extension of its state of exception all reflect the severity of organized-crime penetration and a growing normalization of suspended civil liberties as a governing default.

Haiti's trajectory is diverging sharply from the rest of the region as it approaches a critical inflection point: while Cuba has stabilized enough to warrant a downgrade and the Dominican Republic and Jamaica remain comparatively low-risk, Haiti faces the 30 September expiry of the Gang Suppression Force's mandate, decided by a UN Security Council vote just after this reporting window, which will likely determine whether gang consolidation in Port-au-Prince becomes effectively irreversible within the next 90 days.

countries.name: Venezuela
incidents: 2 Sep — Caribbean/Eastern Pacific: The US 'Southern Spear' campaign continued vessel strikes; the cumulative tally reached at least 230 killed across roughly 70 strikes since the campaign began in September 2025.

2 Sep — Washington: President Trump said Venezuela is 'not ready' for elections and declined to set a timetable, five days after announcing a 100-year, roughly 20%-of-reserves oil concession to a US-linked entity; Venezuela's transitional government disputes the term as 25 years rather than 100.
10–17 Sep — Caribbean/Pacific: No confirmed new US strike on Venezuelan land territory was found for this window; boat-strike operations in international waters continue at pace.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Expect the boat-interdiction campaign to continue at a similar tempo with periodic new strike announcements, while the oil-concession dispute over contract length becomes a persistent friction point between Washington and Caracas' transitional authorities that could stall implementation. Absent a fresh territorial provocation, direct US strikes on Venezuelan soil are unlikely to resume in this window, but political normalization remains indefinitely deferred, sustaining governance uncertainty. Monitor for legal and human-rights fallout from strike video evidence and for any shift in the 25-versus-100-year concession dispute that could reignite unrest.

countries.name: Colombia
incidents: 4 Sep — Ocana, Norte de Santander: An ELN-attributed swarm of roughly 20 explosive-laden drones struck a military compound, killing at least 3 soldiers and wounding 4.
7 Sep — Guamalito, El Carmen, Norte de Santander: A police station was attacked again with explosive drones combined with rifle fire, three days after the Ocana attack.

3 Sep — Cesar department: The US Embassy issued a security alert warning of elevated ELN drone-attack risk; the government rolled out a 'shock plan,' deploying counter-drone systems to five Cesar towns and Valledupar.

Ongoing — Nationwide: The government continues rollout of the roughly $1.68 billion 'Escudo Nacional Antidrones' program, against a backdrop of over 460 drone attacks by armed groups recorded since April 2023.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The ELN/FARC-dissident drone-attack trend is unlikely to abate and will probably continue concentrating in Norte de Santander, Cesar and Cauca, with military and police outposts as primary targets. Government counter-drone deployments will expand but face a capability gap against low-cost, high-volume swarm tactics; expect continued casualties among security forces and growing pressure on the government to demonstrate results from the National Anti-Drone Shield. Watch for possible spillover incidents near the Venezuelan border given cross-border ELN sanctuary dynamics and heightened Southern Spear activity.

countries.name: Haiti
incidents: 23–24 Aug — Kenscoff: A Viv Ansanm-attributed gang attack killed at least 47 people, including 22 reportedly executed at a church compound, and kidnapped 50-plus, displacing over 2,600 residents.

4 Sep — Washington/Port-au-Prince: Haiti's government formally requested the OAS/UN Security Council extend the Gang Suppression Force's mandate through September 2028, presenting a roadmap ahead of the force's 30 September expiry.

Ongoing — Port-au-Prince: Gang coalitions continue to control an estimated 70-85%-plus of the metropolitan area; over 2,000 people have been killed since the start of 2026 and roughly 1.5 million are internally displaced.
30 Sep (imminent) — A UN Security Council vote on Gang Suppression Force mandate renewal is the key event to watch immediately after this reporting period.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained, worsening. The Gang Suppression Force's mandate renewal vote on 30 September is the pivotal near-term event; a lapse or reduced mandate would likely accelerate territorial gains by Viv Ansanm-aligned factions and further erode state presence in and around Port-au-Prince. Even with renewal, force posture appears insufficient to reverse gang control within 90 days. Expect continued mass-casualty attacks on previously safe communes, following the Kenscoff pattern, rising displacement, and near-certain non-viability of December 2026 elections absent a major security inflection.

countries.name: Cuba
incidents: 11 Sep — Nationwide: State utility UNE forecast a roughly 2,000 MW shortfall at Friday peak demand, reflecting continued rolling blackouts.
1 Sep — Nationwide: Blackouts affected roughly 70% of the island simultaneously at the start of the month.
10–17 Sep — Nationwide: No full nationwide grid collapse was identified within the window; the most recent full collapse, the sixth of 2026, occurred 3 August.
Ongoing — Fuel shortages linked to halted Russian shipments and US sanctions pressure remain the structural drivers; sporadic localized protests continue amid the rolling-blackout regime.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Expect continued rolling, multi-hour blackouts without a full grid collapse in the near term, barring a major infrastructure failure or hurricane impact. Localized, sporadic protests are likely to persist at a level below the unrest seen after earlier full collapses. The HIGH rating should hold unless a seventh nationwide collapse occurs or fuel shortages deepen sharply going into Q4.

countries.name: Ecuador
incidents: 15 Sep — Eight provinces and 3 cantons: President Noboa declared a new 60-day state of emergency, suspending inviolability of home and correspondence and authorizing warrantless raids, citing 442 intentional homicides recorded between mid-August and early September.
17–30 Sep — El Oro, Guayas, Los Rios, Manabi: A night curfew from midnight to 5am was imposed.

Ongoing — Manta/Esmeraldas: Deepening US security cooperation continues, with a US Army Special Forces group operating alongside Esmeraldas provincial authorities and naval and air assets deployed to cover the Manta coastal corridor under the 'Shield of the Americas' counter-narcotics coalition.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The new state of emergency and coastal curfew will likely suppress visible crime in curfew zones short-term but risk displacing criminal activity to non-curfewed provinces and rural corridors. Expect continued high homicide rates driven by territorial disputes among trafficking organizations, alongside expanding and increasingly formalized US military presence at Manta and Esmeraldas. Watch for friction between expanded warrantless-search authority and human-rights or legal challenges, and for possible renewal or expansion of the state of emergency if homicide rates do not fall.

countries.name: Peru
incidents: 5 Sep — Five maximum-security prisons (Lima, Tacna, Pasco, La Libertad): A 60-day state of emergency was declared across the facilities, with the military deployed to at least three by the following Monday to sever phone-directed extortion networks.
5 Sep — Junin, Cusco, Ayacucho: States of emergency were declared across 17 districts amid an extortion surge, with additional crackdowns in Piura.
Ongoing — Nationwide: Reported extortion cases rose from 4,761 in 2021 to over 22,000 in 2024, a trend partly attributed to criminal networks including Venezuela's Tren de Aragua.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Expect continued state-of-emergency governance in high-extortion districts and prison facilities, with military-police deployments aimed at severing phone-directed extortion networks. Structural drivers, including prison-based command-and-control and transnational gang presence, are unlikely to be resolved within 90 days, so incremental crackdowns will likely continue without a decisive reduction in extortion case volume.

countries.name: Bolivia
incidents: 11 Sep — La Paz: The government confirmed fuel subsidies will be fully eliminated starting January 2027, part of a $1.9 billion, 36-month IMF financing agreement now before Congress for ratification.
14 Sep — La Paz: The cabinet approved a decree extending the state of exception by a further 90 days.

15 Sep — La Paz: The government stated no blockades were currently in force and warned it would declare a state of siege only if blockades return; sectors in Santa Cruz and Cochabamba were reported threatening new marches and blockades over the diesel subsidy cuts.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Overt Morales-aligned mobilization has receded since June, and the government's extension of the state of exception signals continued vigilance rather than acute crisis. The scheduled January 2027 full subsidy removal is the key forward risk: sectors in Santa Cruz and Cochabamba are already signaling readiness to remobilize over diesel costs, and a renewed blockade wave in Q4 2026 ahead of the subsidy cliff is plausible. Maintain HIGH with a bias toward reassessment if new large-scale blockades materialize.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
incidents: 5 Sep — Independencia province: The Defense Ministry broke ground on a new 14.5 km border-wall segment, part of the 'Frontera Fuerte' project targeting 164 km of barrier along the 391 km Haiti border.
6 Sep — Dajabon: Migration officers detained 58 Haitian nationals in a sweep targeting unauthorized border crossers.
Ongoing — Roughly 79,938 Haitians were deported via the Dajabon crossing alone in the first eight months of 2026, a record pace and a 16.2% year-on-year increase.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Expect continued acceleration of both physical border-hardening and mass deportations of Haitian nationals, likely intensifying as Haiti's security situation deteriorates further ahead of the Gang Suppression Force mandate decision. Human-rights criticism will persist but is unlikely to alter government policy. Internal security risk to the Dominican Republic itself remains low, though migration pressure and diplomatic friction will continue to build.

countries.name: Jamaica
incidents: 16 Sep — St Andrew (Karl Samuda Avenue): Police fatally shot a man known as 'Mad Dog,' prompting residents to mount a burning roadblock on Red Hills Road in protest.
13 Sep — Knightsdale Drive, Kingston 20: A triple-fatality police shooting followed an alleged confrontation with armed individuals.
11 Sep — Lincoln Alley, St Andrew: Police fatally shot a wanted man during an alleged confrontation.
9 Sep — Mount Salem: A wanted man was killed and three police officers injured in a shootout.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. The 2026 homicide-reduction trend, still tracking roughly 40% below 2024, appears to be holding, keeping the overall threat level LOW, but a flagged spike in multiple-fatality police shootings and the 16 September community protest signal rising police-accountability friction that could translate into localized unrest if unaddressed. Watch for continued community protests around high-profile police-involved deaths. Hurricane-season risk remains a parallel, non-conflict hazard through the remainder of the season.
